definitions.explanation: A fabric divider hung at shop entrances, often bearing the shop name or logo.
A business's established reputation and brand value.

examples.english: To pass through the shop curtain.

examples.japanese: お{店|みせ}の{暖簾|のれん}が{風|かぜ}に{揺|ゆ}れている。
examples.english: The shop curtain is swaying in the wind.

examples.japanese: {店先|みせさき}に{新|あたら}しい{暖簾|のれん}を{掛|か}けた。
examples.english: A new curtain was hung at the shop front.

examples.japanese: {暖簾|のれん}を{下|お}ろして、{店|みせ}を{開|ひら}く{準備|じゅんび}をする。
examples.english: To put up the noren and prepare to open the shop.
examples.notes: Putting up the noren signals the shop is open

examples.japanese: この{通|とお}りには{色|いろ}とりどりの{暖簾|のれん}が{並|なら}んでいて、{昔|むかし}ながらの{商店街|しょうてんがい}の{雰囲気|ふんいき}がある。
examples.english: Colorful noren are lined up along this street, giving it the atmosphere of a traditional shopping district.

examples.japanese: {暖簾|のれん}に{傷|きず}がついた。
{暖簾|のれん}{分|わ}けで{独立|どくりつ}する。
examples.notes: Traditional way of letting employees start their own branch under the same name

examples.japanese: {百年|ひゃくねん}{以上|いじょう}の{暖簾|のれん}を{守|まも}り{続|つづ}けている{老舗|しにせ}だ。
examples.english: It's a long-established shop that has maintained its reputation for over a hundred years.

examples.japanese: {創業者|そうぎょうしゃ}が{築|きず}いた{暖簾|のれん}を{次|つぎ}の{世代|せだい}に{引|ひ}き{継|つ}ぐのは{簡単|かんたん}ではない。
examples.english: It's not easy to pass on the reputation built by the founder to the next generation.

notes:
{暖簾|のれん} is a traditional split fabric curtain hung at shop entrances in Japan.

SENSE 1 - PHYSICAL CURTAIN:
- {暖簾|のれん}をくぐる: to pass through (enter a shop)
- {暖簾|のれん}を{下|お}ろす: to put up the noren (open shop)
- {暖簾|のれん}を{上|あ}げる: to take down the noren (close shop)

SENSE 2 - REPUTATION/GOODWILL:
- {暖簾|のれん}を{守|まも}る: to protect the reputation
- {暖簾|のれん}{分|わ}け: branch shop (traditional franchising)
- {暖簾|のれん}に{傷|きず}がつく: to damage one's reputation

IDIOM:
{暖簾|のれん}に{腕押|うでお}し: wasted effort (lit. pushing against a curtain = no resistance, pointless)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Noren display the shop name/logo and signal the business is open. They're iconic in traditional shopping districts.
